citeAs: Mathew, M., Karatzas, D., Jawahar, C.V. (2021). DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar (CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad; Computer Vision Center, UAB)
description: DocVQA is a large-scale dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images, consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The dataset covers a wide variety of document types (letters, forms, reports, tables, etc.) and requires models to read and interpret text within the layout and structure of documents to answer natural language questions.
name: DocVQA
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 independent annotations per question (stage 1 and stage 2 workers each provide answers independently; a third review stage is applied when stage 1 and stage 2 answers do not match)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer mismatches between stage 1 and stage 2 annotations triggered a third-stage review by the authors. Questions flagged as inapt (due to language issues or ambiguity) were excluded from the dataset. Human performance was measured at 94.36% accuracy (ANLS 0.981) on the test split, serving as an upper bound.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom web-based annotation tool (remote workers); annotation effort supported by Amazon
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages: (1) Workers were shown a document image and asked to define up to 10 question-answer pairs, entering answers verbatim from the document; workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question where warranted. (2) A second worker was shown the image and questions (but not the answers from stage 1), required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question; workers could flag questions as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity. (3) If no answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review by the authors, who could edit questions/answers or ignore them.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is sourced exclusively from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, covering only 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical). Many documents are from the food and nutrition collections because they have a higher proportion of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960–2000 period. A large majority of questions start with "what is the", asking for dates, titles, totals, amounts or names. Almost all top answers are numeric values due to the prevalence of reports and invoices.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, downloaded from different collections across 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical). Pages were hand-picked from 6,071 industry documents spanning documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018. Binarized images were minimized; pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized. Questions and answers were collected via remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage process.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents across 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical). Documents include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text, covering a wide variety of document types such as letters, forms, reports, agendas, memos, scientific reports, transaction documents, tables, publications, financial reports, telephone records, contracts, articles, emails, graphics, notes, budgets, minutes, photographs, and invoices.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Source documents span from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018; most documents are from the 1960–2000 period.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: OCR errors can result in incorrect answers even when models correctly ground questions to the relevant image region. The dataset is limited to documents from 5 specific industries from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Most documents are from the 1960–2000 period. Binarization of many source documents affected image quality. Existing models perform significantly below human performance (94.36%), especially on questions requiring understanding of figures, photographs, and handwriting.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Binarized images were minimized to avoid poor image quality being a bottleneck. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application and serialized in top-left to bottom-right order. Data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train (39,463 questions, 10,194 images), validation (5,349 questions, 1,286 images), and test (5,188 questions, 1,287 images) splits.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to inspire a "purpose-driven" approach in document image analysis and recognition research, enabling intelligent reading systems that can respond to ad-hoc information requests expressed in natural language. This could drive practical applications in document understanding at scale.
rai:dataUseCases: Visual Question Answering on document images; benchmarking document understanding models; driving purpose-driven Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research; evaluating models that combine visual and textual cues for reading and interpreting document structure (tables, forms, figures, handwriting).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A commercial OCR application was used to extract OCR tokens from document images for use in baselines and upper bound computations.

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper does not describe demographics of the remote workers who performed annotation.

null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation or augmentation protocol is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan is described beyond mentioning a leaderboard at docvqa.org.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper does not discuss personal or sensitive information in the dataset.
